lenses.summary: GLOBAL CHROME AND LAYOUT lens. The preview's chrome doesn't follow core anywhere. Wordmark, nav labels, order and alignment, header CTA, sign-in, mobile navigation, footer, page background, band rhythm, hero geometry, container width, gutters and breakpoints all differ from the core PublicShell (client/src/clarity/PublicShell.tsx -> components/Navbar.tsx + components/Footer.tsx + the index.css clarity block at lines 1250-1487 and the container tokens at lines 64-93). Measured left content edges at 1440: core uses one edge for header, hero, sections and footer (x=116 to 1323, rendered by .container-x). The preview has four: header x=64 to 1381, hero x=101, sections x=80 to 1359, footer x=72. Background bands measured at x=5 confirm the structure. Core home runs white and #F4F4F5 bands alternately, with one #0D0D0D closing CTA at y 8004-8486. The preview home runs cream (245,241,233) with a #181619 hero at y 110-1010 and taupe (40,36,36) full-bleed bands at y 2656-3364 and 5396-7198. Smallest overall fix: replace the preview's .site-header, .site-footer, .content-width and .page-shell with a static mirror of PublicShell (copy Navbar PRIMARY/AUDIENCE_MENUS/actions/Menu drawer, the Footer GROUPS and copyright, and the --paper/--container-max/--container-gutter tokens and breakpoints). Keep the prototype bar as an overlay that holds the review switcher. Then let imagery vary only inside core sections. Five core-internal inconsistencies go to the core lane: (1) the assisted-order catalog uses 16px/10px gutters instead of container-x; (2) research pages carry two navigation rows; (3) five different wordmarks and shells; (4) the footer brand name is hidden below 520px; (5) three different sub-nav patterns. Capture notes: the core reference screenshots include the PWA install toast at bottom centre (a runtime overlay, not drift). The core mobile drawer and the 834 tablet layout are evidenced from source only; no core capture exists for them. Crops are in C:\Users\sboad\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--xenios-wt-general-platform\6abf1edf-2b16-476e-8305-23b9a0014e06\scratchpad\ui_drift\agent-crops\chrome\. No repository files were edited.

lenses.summary:
Typography and tokens lens. Result: the private founder preview does not use the core Xenios type system or token set anywhere. I found 21 material drifts, 8 minor drifts, 5 allowed-exploration items worth keeping and 6 core-internal inconsistencies.

Root causes:
1. preview.css ships no webfont. Its stack (Inter, "Helvetica Neue", Arial) fell back to Arial in every capture. Core self-hosts Inter Tight 500-900 and JetBrains Mono through client/src/fonts.ts.
2. preview.css:1-16 reuses core token names with different values: --paper is cream #f5f1e9 instead of #FFFFFF, --ink is #111113 instead of #0E0E0E, --teal is #52c9b8 instead of #14B8C7. It also adds warm --ivory, --taupe and --purple, plus about 20 hard-coded warm grays.
3. Headings run on their own scale. At 1440 the hero h1 is 106.6px at weight 570 with -0.055em tracking; core's display-l is 76px, weight 800, -0.022em. At 390 the preview is 58.5px against core's 32px. The preview also adds gradient-clipped text, which appears nowhere in core.
4. Eyebrows are 11px Arial 800 with a gradient dash; core uses JetBrains Mono .mono-cap in --pulse or --ink-mute. The preview labels are 9-12px; core's smallest public text is 12px (mono) or 14px (body-s). The preview has none of core's purple underlined text links.
5. Buttons are 999px pills, 42px high, 12px text; core .btn is 4px radius, 64px desktop / 56px mobile, 15-16px weight 700. The preview's radius scale (32/22/20px) and soft shadows have no counterpart in clarity, whose maximum is 18px with flat cards.

Smallest overall fix: delete preview.css's :root, element and component rules for these areas. Load a pinned snapshot of core client/src/index.css and fonts.ts at runtime c0e25c73, then build each section from the clarity primitives (PublicPage, ContentSection, InfoCard, ActionLink, BoundaryNote, NumberedSteps, Footer, Navbar) and the research card and badge components. Keep imagery as the only free variable.

The core-lane decisions are covered in the core-internal rows.

Lens: catalog and product cards. The preview's catalog card is a separate component and does not mirror the core card. lenses.summary: PAGE-SURFACES LENS. Verdict: the founder preview is a separate website. None of its customer pages matches its nearest core surface in structure. Crops are in scratchpad/ui_drift/agent-crops/page-surfaces/ (sbs_*.png, ov_*.png, core_cards_*.png, mobile_top_4up*.png). Four facts every approver needs: (1) The current core public UI contains no imagery at all. Home.tsx, clarity/pages.tsx, CarePublicPages.tsx and the assisted-order cards have no . RotatingHero and the .grad-0x presets are not used on any live page. The only core image slot is CatalogDiscoveryCard (master-offerings/CatalogDiscoveryPresentation.tsx:105-115), which no route uses. So every image placement in the preview is a proposed addition and must be shown as a slot inside a named core component. (2) Core has no public Featured page, no Coming-soon page or section, no public product detail page (/products/:slug renders "We couldn't find that product.") and no Care product grid. The preview invents all four as journeys. (3) Core /products is a text pathway page with no grid. The real public product-card surface is /research/early-access/order-request (AssistedOrderPage). It has a Research sub-nav, a 4-step stepper, Family/Action filters, a 2-up card grid with a 340px "Your request" rail, and pagination. The preview drops all of that. (4) Status, account and support are separate core pages: StatusPage, SignIn, SupportPage, AccountOrdersView, AssistedOrderStatusPage and CustomerQuotePanel. The preview collapses them into one invented page. Home: 9 of the 11 core sections are missing and 6 are invented. The hero is a dark full-bleed band with a 106px gradient-text headline and Products-first pill CTAs. Core uses a white display-l 76px/800 hero with Care-first 4px-radius buttons. Care: the page invents steps and a product grid, and omits the core status card, "What Care is not", the emergency boundary and the 911 footer line. Held, quote and research detail views use invented chip labels and CTAs. Examples: Formulation held / View hold details versus core Temporarily Unavailable with no CTA; Quote only / Request a quote versus core Request pricing. Core-internal issues for the core lane to settle before the preview can mirror a single target: - The assisted-order catalog is a token island: green ink and accent, pill buttons, 16px gutters and a 67px/700 h1, versus clarity's black/white, 4px buttons and display-l. - Core has at least three card/detail anatomies (xenios-order-card, MasterOfferingCard/Detail, CatalogDiscoveryCard). - Card radius is inconsistent: .card is 4px, .clarity-card is 18px. - Hero scale varies across pages: 76, 51.2, 35 and 67px. - Research pages carry two nav layers, an alternate footer, and two brand names ("Xenios" vs "Xenios Health"). - The catalog's Action filter labels differ from its card chip labels. Recommended order: 1. The core lane names the canonical card, detail and catalog surface. 2. Rebuild the preview pages as mirrors of the named core pages, in their exact section order. 3. Re-insert imagery only through the allowed slots (rows PS-A1 to PS-A7). 4. Move all QA scaffolding (truth strip, boundary, calibration, QA and wireframe links, Visual class/state facts) out of customer page bodies and nav. Read-only review: no repository files were edited and no servers or browsers were started.

lenses.summary:
Lens: copy, navigation and route truth. I checked the preview (8b06da5) against the real core client (closeout-review 8549011, runtime c0e25c73), its screenshots and the assisted-order source. The preview's catalog-data.js was missing from preview-src, so I pulled catalog-data.json from git object 8b06da5 into agent-crops/copy-nav/preview-catalog-data-8b06da5.json to get the real pathway, price and CTA strings. Crops are in C:\Users\sboad\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--xenios-wt-general-platform\6abf1edf-2b16-476e-8305-23b9a0014e06\scratchpad\ui_drift\agent-crops\copy-nav\.

Headline: almost nothing in the preview's chrome, copy or routes matches production. An approver would be misled on the brand lockup, the whole navigation, the header and hero actions, the homepage purpose, and where products live.

What core actually does:
- **Brand:** the public chrome says "Xenios" (BRAND.publicName).
- **Navigation and actions:** the desktop nav is For Individuals, For Practices, Partners, How It Works, Quality, About and Careers. The header actions are Sign In plus Start Care. Mobile adds a Menu overlay.
- **Care first:** the hero and every main call-to-action lead with Care.
- **Products:** `/products` is a pathway explainer with no product grid. The catalog sits behind an invitation password at `/research/early-access`, and the order flow is at `/research/early-access/order-request`.
- **Product detail:** there is no public detail page. `/products/:slug` shows "We couldn't find that product." Detail is the "Product details" panel that expands inside each card.
- **Card wording:**
  - Badges: Order request, Care pathway, Request pricing, Request Order, Temporarily Unavailable.
  - Buttons: Add to order request, Continue through Care, Request pricing.
  - Prices: a dollar amount, "Price on request", or "Ask the Care team about pricing".
  - Held items have no button.
- **Status:** `/status`, `/sign-in` and `/support` are separate pages, and Care status is never shown with research orders.
- **Required notices:** every research card carries "Research Use Only. Not for human or veterinary use." Care pages carry the emergency notice and the "call 911" footer line.

None of these appear in the preview. It invents its own versions:
- Pages and nav items: Featured, Status & account, QA grid, Explore catalog, Coming soon.
- Card states and buttons: Research access, View product, Quote only / Request a quote, Formulation held / View hold details, Binding pending.
- Price wording: Care pricing withheld, Price omitted from static preview.
- A standalone product detail page, product cards on the Care page, and a combined status/account page that lists a Care intake next to research orders.

Customer-facing text also uses internal terms (commerce authority, Runtime Product Control, canonical row, binding) and fixed counts (423, 242, 426/424). The preview never mentions research use, emergencies, 911 or medical advice.

Things that already match core and should be kept: the "Care pathway" badge, "Price on request" on quote-only items, the "Xenios Care" eyebrow, and the words "Coming soon".

Core is inconsistent with itself in five places. The core lane should decide these before the preview copies any of them:
- **Brand name:** core variously uses Xenios, Xenios Care, Xenios Health and Xenios Research.
- **One research state, three names:** "Direct Order", "Order request" and "Add to order request" all mean the same thing, with mixed capitalisation.
- **Two nav bars on Research pages:** the second bar uses different casing and links to `/research/*` addresses that redirect.
- **"Explore Products" goes to two places:** `/products` and `/research/early-access`.
- **Price wording:** the member catalog wording differs from the assisted-order catalog wording.

The preview should mirror the assisted-order catalog wording, because that is the route actually in use for launch.

addedRows.preview: No body weight is set, so all running text renders at 400 (preview.css:17-21, 31-39). Headings use 570/580 (preview.css:252, 260), buttons 750 (168), the brand 850 (114), pills and labels 800. With core's font payload these would render as 600, 800 and 900.
addedRows.drift: Spec lines, price lines, panel paragraphs and footer copy all read a step lighter than production. The preview's intermediate weights can't be reproduced by production's font files, so the ramp the founder approves isn't one production can render.
addedRows.correction: Mirror the core baseline: import core's fonts.ts set (the same @fontsource files), use body weight 500, and use only weights 500 to 900, preferably through core's typography classes (display-*, h2, body-*, mono-label) rather than numeric weights.

coreInconsistencies: Canonical brand name and wordmark: core uses several names and lockups across the global clarity shell, research shell and page titles ('Xenios', 'xenios', 'Private document, xenios'). See CI-3 (chrome), CI-1 (copy-nav), PS-K5. The preview's 'Xenios Health' has partial precedent until the core lane names one.
Research public pages render two navigation systems, with label, casing and destination drift between them: CI-2 (chrome), CI-3 (copy-nav), PS-K5.
There is no single section sub-navigation component; core uses three patterns (CI-5 chrome).
The footer brand name is hidden below 520px because the header rule `.clarity-brand-name` sr-only (index.css:1459-1460) also applies to the footer (CI-4 chrome).
Hero and H1 scale: core has four treatments along one journey (clarity 76px/800 vs assisted-order 67.2px/700 at desktop, per core-capture-receipt.json). See CORE-01, PS-K4.

The assisted-order catalog is a token island: green-black ink, sage accent, pill buttons, 12-22px radii, green eyebrow. Its width also ignores container-x. See CORE-02, CC-35, PS-K1, CI-1 (chrome), CC-38.
Card radius and primitive: core uses 4px (.card/.tile, index.css:484-505), 18px (.clarity-card, .xenios-order-card) and a 22px panel. See CORE-03, PS-K3.

Product-card and product-detail anatomies: there are three card anatomies (assisted-order, EarlyAccessProductCard, member catalog / Featured) and at least three gated detail anatomies (MemberProductDetailExperience, FullCatalogProductRoute, catalog-display/ProductDetail, plus Kris). See CC-34, PS-K2, ADD-03.

State badges and vocabulary: there is no canonical badge style (CORE-04). Status and action labels are inconsistent (CC-37, CI-2 copy-nav), filter labels don't match chip labels (PS-K6), raw family codes appear beside friendly labels (CC-36), price wording differs between catalog surfaces (CI-5 copy-nav), and 'Explore Products' has two destinations (CI-4 copy-nav).

Accent system: the clarity system does not sanction a purple-to-teal accent (CORE-05), yet index.css still carries dead purple-to-blue-to-teal tokens (.grad-0x, .gradient-pill, --pill-1 to --pill-4) that nothing routed uses (ADD-10).
The body-xs class used on research card micro-text is undefined (CORE-06).
Form controls and focus: there are three field systems (input-field on /sign-in, clarity-field on /support and /status, assisted-order fields on the catalog) and four focus-ring treatments (ADD-07).
Font weights: clarity CSS declares 650/750/850, but only static 500 to 900 files are loaded, so they render as 700/800/900 (ADD-08).
Status timelines: core uses clarity-status-timeline on public /status and xenios-order-timeline on assisted-order status and confirmation (ADD-09).

Imagery policy: EarlyAccessProductCard states no product photography, while gated member catalog and detail surfaces render Product Control media at 4:3 contain with a pending fallback (ADD-11, CC-39). This must be decided before any imagery approval is production-meaningful.
